name: Brazil Minas Gerais Luzia Natural
tags: Brazil, Essentials, Green Coffee, Natural Process, Perennial
varieties: Various (Mundo Novo, Yellow catuai, Topazio, Acaia)
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of nougat and cashew. Flavors of caramel, chocolate and cream with an aftertaste of dried dates and sweet nuttiness. Very mild citric acidity with a creamy, medium body and soft mouthfeel.
roasting_notes:
Like many natural processed Brazilian coffee, low and slow is our preferred approach with Luzia. The coffee tastes best when sweetness and body are accentuated by a longer roast with higher end temperatures. We find a solid medium roast to be the perfect fit for this coffee, although we have been enjoying its clean and sweet aftertaste on light cupping roasts. Excellent for espresso or adding into blends.

name: Colombia EA "Sugarcane" Decaf
tags: Colombia, Decaf, Essentials, Green Coffee, Perennial, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of cocoa butter and cherry with up front notes of fudge, vanilla and cocoa butter, aftertaste of orange and cherry, medium malic acidity, heavy body and juicy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: Like many EA decafs, we feel like the sweet spot with this is right in the middle of a medium roast. The density is relatively high as well as the moisture content so expect to throw some heat at this coffee with your machine. The sweetness of this coffee tends to show itself best with a longer development.

name: Ethiopia Guji Firē G3 Natural 2025
region: Benti Korba Kebele, Oddoo Shakiso Woreda, Guji, Oromia
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Natural Process, Organically Grown, Perennial
tasting_notes: Fragrance of cherry and pomegranate followed by dark chocolate. Flavors of cherry and mixed red fruits with an aftertaste of honey, dark chocolate and orange. Mild citric acidity, creamy mouthfeel and heavy body.
roasting_notes: This coffee is all about the fruit, chocolate and body. We recommend roasting close to medium (about 80 to 85 Agtron) for a “big” and heavy fruit-forward cup profile.

name: Ethiopia Guji Shakiso Gigesa Natural
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Natural Process, Organically Grown, Perennial
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of dark chocolate, strawberry and florals with notes of grape, strawberry, and milk chocolate. Aftertaste of black tea, honey and rose with a mild citric and lactic acidity and a juicy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: The coffee from Gigesa shines at multiple roast levels. Keep it light (about 100 to 110 Agtron) for more berry notes or take to a light-medium to medium roast (about 80 to 100 Agtron) to highlight the chocolate notes and heavy mouthfeel. Tastes great in blends and even better as a single origin espresso.

name: Guatemala Finca El Socorro Juan Diego de la Cerda Maracaturra
tags: Green Coffee, Guatemala, Rare, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of yuzu and florals. Notes of dark chocolate, starfruit, citrus fruit and cocoa with an aftertaste of pear and green apple. Bright citric acidity and a medium body with creamy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: We recommend keeping this coffee roasted light (about 95 to 105 Agtron) to preserve the delicate fruit and soft floral notes that make this coffee so interesting! The large maracaturra seeds benefit from a slower, more gentle roast approach to evenly roast through the center.
watchlist_notes: 700ha; 400ha preserved forest; hot water fermentation preserves sugars/density

name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Aricha Adorsi Washed
region: Aricha Woreda, Yirgacheffe, Gedeo Zone, SNNPR
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Perennial, Washed Process
tasting_notes:
Lemon blossom and black pepper fragrance followed by the aroma of goldenberry. Flavors of mango, lemon and floral with a sweet lingering aftertaste of matcha, raw cocoa, watermelon and white grape. Mild to bright acidity of citric and malic acids with a juicy mouthfeel and medium body. 
.
roasting_notes: This is a very versatile coffee. We love keeping this coffee from Aricha at a light roast (about 95 to 105 Agtron) to maintain those delicate fruit and floral notes. At medium roasts (about 75 to 85 Agtron) the sweetness and tea notes tend to shine through with a bittersweet profile.

name: El Salvador Finca Colomba Agua Nueva Bourbon Semi Wash 2025
region: Los Naranjos, Ilamatepec, Santa Ana Department
tags: El Salvador, Essentials, Green Coffee, Perennial, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Butterscotch and floral fragrance and aroma, sweet flavors of caramel, honey and nougat. Clean aftertaste of green apple, nougat, orange and rose. Soft citric and malic acid. Heavy body with silky mouthfeel.
roasting_notes:
Best at the darker end of a light roast up to a full dark roast. The coffee has a great range and 
excellent sweetness. Stands out on its own, but can also fortify any blend with sweetness and body.

name: Ethiopia Guji Shakiso Gigesa Washed
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Organically Grown, Perennial, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of orange blossom and peach with notes of milk chocolate and peach with an aftertaste of green grape, orange and florals. Bright lactic and malic acidity with a light body and tea-like mouthfeel. Delicate and delicious!
roasting_notes:
Somewhere between light and light-medium roast is the sweet spot for this coffee from Guji this year. The complex acidity is delicious and the sweetness is prevalent even in very light roasts. For the full bouquet of notes, try roasting light (about 90-95 Agtron). For more cooked sugary notes, such as caramel, and less tea-like notes, try pushing into medium roast territory (about 80 to 90 Agtron). 
Check out our Roast Approach on this coffee here.

name: Ethiopia Sidama Ayla Bombe Natural
region: Bombe Kebele, Bensa Woreda, Sidama Zone
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Natural Process, Organically Grown, Perennial
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of orange blossom, plum and strawberry. Sweet up front flavors of strawberry, lavender and vanilla with an aftertaste of cherry, lemon and florals. Bright citric and malic acidity with a light-medium body and milky mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: Avoid too much heat in the beginning of the roast. We find that this natural is has a lot of delicate floral notes paired with the classic fruit notes found in natural processed coffee from Sidama. Keeping the roast light (about 95-110 Agtron) will keep these floral notes intact while pushing the roast darker will accentuate more jammy fruit notes.

name: India Ratnagiri Estate Kere Patte Anaerobic Mossto Washed
tags: anaerobic, Green Coffee, India, Innovative, Sequential Processing, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of chocolate, lychee and plum. Unique notes of black currant, grape and  milk chocolate with an aftertaste of cocoa powder, prune and white chocolate. Medium malic and lactic acidity with a medium body and smooth, tea-like mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: Roasting this coffee to lighter degrees will bring out the black currant and malic grape qualities.  As the coffee roasts with more development, the notes of chocolate and cocoa will become even more prominent in the cup.

name: Ethiopia Sidama Ayla Shantawene Washed
region: Shantawane, Bombe Kebele, Bensa Woreda, Sidama Zone
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Organically Grown, Perennial, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of cocoa and honeysuckle. Notes of watermelon and white peach with an aftertaste of yuzu, lime, camomile and jasmine. Mild malic and tartaric acidity with a soft/round mouthfeel and medium body.
roasting_notes: The complexity of this fully washed coffee really comes through at the light to light-medium roast range (about 95-110 Agtron). The higher density coffee can take some heat in the beginning but the seeds are on the smaller size so watch out for the temperature taking off near and after the first crack.

name: Costa Rica Hacienda Sonora Diego Guardia Dwarf Caturra Natural
region: Carrillos Alto de Poás, Alajuela, Central Valley
tags: Costa Rica, Green Coffee, Natural Process
tasting_notes:
Absolutely wild! Really unique fragrance and aroma coming from lactic fermentation. In terms of color we note blue, green, purple and pink. The flavors resemble the fragrance and aroma with a surprisingly clean aftertaste like sour green apple candy. The lactic acidity is very forward with some malic acidity behind it. Medium body with soft mouthfeel. 

Definitely a unique and “funky” coffee!
roasting_notes: The coffee needs a strong amount of heat energy through Maillard to progress.  Look for this coffee to have a later first crack and to really take off right before first crack.  As you are dialing in this coffee, you may see the first crack temperature bounce around depending on the heat application during earlier phases of the roast.  At lighter roasts, you’ll find the bright and complex lactic acidity.  Further advancement through the roast will decrease the acidity and enhance the sweetness of the coffee.

name: Guatemala Antigua El Pesadero Jauja Stuardo Coto
region: San Cristobal el Bajo aldea, Antigua Municipality
tags: Essentials, Green Coffee, Guatemala, Perennial, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of dark chocolate and elderberry. Notes of dark chocolate, lemongrass and citrus fruit with a sweet aftertaste of cream, grape and pomegranate. Medium citric and malic acidity with a juicy mouthfeel and medium-heavy body.
roasting_notes: Coming soon

name: Colombia Risaralda Pereira Finca Milán Caturra Nitro Watermelon Infused
tags: Co-fermentation, Colombia, Experimental, Green Coffee
farmer_grower: Julio César Madrid Tisnés and Julio Andrés Quiceno
tasting_notes: Watermelon, watermelon, watermelon! This watermelon infusion/co-ferment delivers it’s namesake. We also note cantaloupe, watermelon candy and other melon notes with a mild lactic acidity and a medium body with a creamy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: We recommend roasting this coffee at a light roast with a quick approach through Maillard reaction to pop the complex fruit acidity.  A shorter post crack development time will preserve the fresh sweetness.  In our experience, these types of alternative processed coffees can have a very quiet first crack.

name: Colombia Tolima Regional Excelso
tags: Colombia, Essentials, Green Coffee, Perennial, washed, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance of cherry, chocolate, and soft orange blossom with a wet aroma of dark chocolate and hazelnut.  The cup has flavors of rich chocolate, sweet panela sugar, and nougat.  A medium citric acidity is balanced with a heavy body and dark chocolate finish.
roasting_notes: This washed Colombian coffee is incredibly versatile and lends itself to a multitude of roasting profiles.  At a lighter roast, the coffee will have a prominent juicy citric acidity and raw sugar sweetness.  To achieve this cup character, utilize a higher charge temperature and heavy heat application.  This is a high density washed coffee that can handle high heat.  At a medium roast, the coffee will exhibit more of the chocolate and nutty notes.  The raw sugar sweetness will transform into notes of caramel and the acidity will be reduced.  The dark chocolate finish will become more pronounced.  To achieve this cup profile, you will want to extend time spent in the caramelization (late Maillard) as well as extending the post crack development time.  This is also a coffee that will do very well in a dark roast.  The dark roast will bring forward the flavors of dark chocolate, deep caramelized sugars, roasted nuts, and some brown spice.  This cup profile will have muted acidity and a thinner body.  To achieve this cup profile, focus on extending the post crack development time with a steady rate of rise.  In the final stages of a dark roast, the coffee will need very little heat energy to continue the roasting process.

name: Rwanda Nyamasheke Muhororo Ireme Anaerobic Natural
tags: anaerobic, Green Coffee, Rwanda
farmer_grower: Celestin and Marie Rumenerangabo and 236 other households
tasting_notes: ​Fragrance and aroma of pineapple, cocoa, rum and dark fruits. Notes of dark chocolate, vanilla, and black cherry with an aftertaste of dark fruits. Medium malic and acetic acidity with a heavy body and syrupy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: This anaerobic coffee has a wide range of flavors. We recommend roasting to a medium-light roast for a cup with lively acidity (about 95 Agtron). For more syrupy profiles and brewing as espresso, we suggest trying a medium-medium roast for maximum sweetness and fruit notes with a more muted acidity (about 75 to 85 Agtron).

name: Guatemala Huehuetenango Chq'Ul Armando Gomez Sauco 2025
tags: Essentials, Green Coffee, Guatemala, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of dark chocolate, plum and whipped cream. Notes of elderberry, white grape and browned butter with an aftertaste of dark chocolate, nougat and chardonnay. Medium malic and citric acidity with a medium body and soft, smooth mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: Armando’s coffee tastes amazing in just about every which way. At light roasts those delicate flavors and aftertaste are maintained while at medium roasts the chocolates and dark fruits come forward, still maintaining that buttery mouthfeel. Darker roasts will mute much of the nuance but you are sure for a sweet cup! Check out our Roast Approach on this coffee here.

name: India Ratnagiri Estate Godown Patte Catuai Cavery Natural
tags: Essentials, Green Coffee, India, Natural Process, Sequential Processing
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of brown sugar and dark fruits. Notes of cocoa powder and raisin with an aftertaste of cooked blueberry, rooibos tea and sweet bread pastry. Medium malic and acetic acidity with a medium-heavy body and smooth mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: With this natural processed coffee, roasting to a lighter roast with shorter post crack development will accentuate the malic acidity and fruit notes.  When given more development, the sweet notes of cooked fruit and brown sugar will be highlighted, while also developing more body.

name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Aricha Adorsi Premium Black Honey
region: Aricha Woreda, Yirgacheffe, Gedeo Zone, SNNPR
tags: Ethiopia, Experimental, Green Coffee, Honey Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of dark chocolate, red currant, orange zest. Notes of green grape, pineapple, cherry and orange. Aftertaste of dark chocolate, red apple and red currant. Bright malic acidity with a syrupy mouthfeel and medium body.
roasting_notes: Coming soon.

name: Swiss Water Decaf Rwanda Nyamasheke Muhororo Natural
tags: Decaf, Green Coffee, Natural Process, Rwanda, Swiss Water Decaf
farmer_grower: Celestin and Marie Rumenerangabo and 236 other households
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of raisin, black cherry and red currant. Notes of cherry and chocolate with an aftertaste of green apple and honeycomb sweetness. Bright malic acidity and a light-medium body with milky mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: Swiss Water processed decaffeinated coffees will lose their moisture more easily at the beginning of a roast. Use a gentle approach at the early stages of the roast to retain moisture needed for chemical reactions later in the roasting process. Longer development times will bring forward more sweetness in the coffee, while a short development time will accentuate the coffee’s complex fruit character and soft florality. Check out this roasting guide provided by Swiss Water Decaf.

name: India Ratnagiri Estate Giri Patte Catuai Sequential Washed
tags: Essentials, Green Coffee, India, Sequential Processing, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of chocolate and fig with notes of caramel and lime. Sweet aftertaste of rooibos tea with a mild citric acidity and silky mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: When roasting this sequential washed lot of the Catuai variety, we recommend approaching this coffee as you would a washed central.  This coffee has an exceptional amount of sweetness that allows for dynamic sugar development when the caramelization phase of the roast is extended before first crack.  With a shorter caramelization, the roast will accentuate the citric acidity.

name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Kochere G1 Natural
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Natural Process, New Arrival, Organically Grown
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of boysenberry, orange blossom and cocoa. Notes of berries, fruity pebbles with a floral aftertaste. Medium orange-like acidity with a medium, milky body and a sugary, fruit-like sweetness.
roasting_notes: For roasting this Ethiopian natural processed coffee, we recommend a lighter roast to preserve the fresh berry character of the cup and the floral aromatics.  A softer charge temperature will allow heat to evenly penetrate the dense bean, higher heat application through Maillard reaction will develop the complex acidity that brings the bright berry flavor forward.  Stretching out the period of time spent in the caramelization phase (20-30 degrees prior to first crack) will transform vibrant fresh berry flavors into rich sweet flavors of jam while enhancing the body.  Finishing the roast, we recommend a short period of time in post crack development to preserve sweetness and acidity.  For more dark chocolate notes, extend the time spent in post crack development.

name: Ethiopia West Arsi Werka Nensebo Washed
region: Werka Village, Refisa Kebele, Nensebo District, West Arsi, Oromia
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Organically Grown, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of brown sugar, lemon blossom and vanilla. Notes of lavender, peach and pear with an aftertaste of black tea, honey and brown sugar. Mild malic acidity with a juicy mouthfeel and heavy body.
roasting_notes: The complexity of this fully washed coffee really comes through at the light-medium roast range (about 95-100 Agtron). Roasting lighter (about 105-110 Agtron) will present more florals and more pronounced fruit notes. Pushing into medium roast territory (about 80 Agtron) will yield a very sweet profile with that brown sugar and honey sweetness prevalent.

name: Burundi Kayanza Nemba Natural
tags: Burundi, Green Coffee, Natural Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of blackberry, black cherry and strawberry jam. Notes of black currant and strawberry followed by an aftertaste of blood orange and cocoa powder with a cooked fruit sweetness. Bright malic and citric acidity with a medium-heavy body and syrupy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: The coffees from Kibingo are all very versatile. Light-medium roasts (about 85 to 100 Agtron) accentuate the bright citrus acidity and unique fruit notes while solid medium roasts (about 75 to 85 Agtron) show more of the vanilla and chocolate characteristics.

name: Guatemala Palencia Finca La Pia Victor Calderón La Aurora
region: La Joya Larga, Palencia, Fraijanes Plateau Region, Guatemala
tags: Essentials, Green Coffee, Guatemala, Organically Grown, Perennial, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Clove and dark chocolate noted in fragrance and aroma with notes of dark chocolate, florals and stonefruit followed by an aftertaste of fresh cream, baking spices and black tea. Bright and complex acidity with citric, malic and lactic acid noted. Medium body with a tea-like mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: We recommend keeping Don Victor’s La Aurora lot in the light to medium roast range (about 85 to 95 Agtron). The sweetness and spices are at the forefront of this cup profile but the delicate acidity shines in the lighter roasts.

name: Honduras Lempira San Andrés Finca La Puerta Ruben Portillo Washed
tags: Essentials, Green Coffee, Honduras, Perennial, washed, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of cherry, chocolate and brown sugar. Up front notes of chocolate with a sweetness of molasses and florals. Aftertaste of dark chocolate with a mild citric acidity. Medium-heavy body and a creamy, almost fudge-like mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: This Honduran coffee is straightforward to roast. Average density and moisture content set this up to be fairly predictable. We love the brown sugar sweetness and other sugary notes in this coffee which are accentuated in the light-medium to medium-dark roast range (about 80 to 65 Agtron). The acidity is mellow, but present on the lighter end of that spectrum so the coffee really allows you to dial in the profile to meet your specific preferences.

name: Guatemala Acatenango Finca El Mirador Stuardo Coto Gesha Washed
tags: gesha, Green Coffee, Guatemala, Rare, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of rose and pomegranate with a sweet up front flavor of vanilla and white cake. Unique aftertaste of banana and milk chocolate with a mild acidity and a soft, coating mouthfeel and heavy body.
roasting_notes: To best pull out the delicate floral notes in the fragrance and finish, we recommend a light roast.  High heat application and a higher charge temperature will bring out the tropical fruit character in the coffee.

name: Rwanda Nyamasheke Muhororo Natural
tags: Green Coffee, Natural Process, Rwanda
farmer_grower: Celestin and Marie Rumenerangabo and 236 other households
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of cooked fruit, and cherry. Up front flavors of cherry, chocolate, and florals. Aftertaste of grape, raisin and apple with a honey-like sweetness. Medium malic acidity. Medium body with a milky mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: This coffee has a lot of delicate notes that will shine best in the range of light roasts (about 90 to 110 Agtron). Medium roasts will lose much of the floral notes and present a clean and sweet cup.

name: Guatemala Acatenango Finca El Mirador Stuardo Coto Pacamara Natural
tags: Green Coffee, Guatemala, Natural Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of blackberry and dark chocolate. Up front notes of blackberry, blueberry and strawberry, with an aftertaste of dark chocolate and citrus fruit. Medium malic acidity and a medium body with a creamy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: We enjoy this coffee roasted light to medium (around 95 to 75 Agtron) to focus on the unique acidity and sweetness in the cup. The Pacamara is a very large bean size so lower heat settings might be needed during roasting to achieve an even roast from the outside to the inside of the bean. Check out our 2026 Roast Approach on this coffee here.

name: Ethiopia Sidama Arbegona Duwancho Premium Natural
tags: Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Rare, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance of strawberry, aroma of dark chocolate and orange blossom. Sweet and sugary with notes of cocoa nib, pomegranate and strawberry and an aftertaste of orange blossom and tannins. Medium malic and lactic acidity with a heavy body and creamy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: Coming soon!

name: Mexico Chiapas Finca Nuevo Mexico Bayunka Semi-Washed
tags: Essentials, Green Coffee, Mexico, New Arrival, semi-washed
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of caramel, brown sugar and nutty with up front notes of milk chocolate and florals. Brown sugar sweetness and a nutty aftertaste. Mild citric acidity and a medium body with a soft mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: This coffee from Finca Nuevo México boasts big chocolate notes with a really heavy body. We recommend roasting somewhere between light-medium and medium (about 70-85 Agtron). Excellent for espresso and for holding a great base in blends.

name: India Kerehaklu Estate S9 Blossom Cultured Washed
tags: Essentials, Green Coffee, India, Inoculated, Sequential Processing, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of dark chocolate, florals, and dark spices. Up front notes of milk chocolate and lavender with an aftertaste of lime zest and sweet maltiness. Medium citric and malic acidity with a heavy body and creamy mouthfeel. Overall well-balanced!
roasting_notes: The balance and versatility of this coffee means that it can perform well at a lot of different roast levels. We recommend approaching this with high heat up front and backing off later in the roast to stretch Maillard and Caramelization a bit. The seeds look and feel a bit like high grown African or Guatemalan coffees. The character of the coffee reminds us of the washed Muhororo coffee from Rwanda and the resulting cup is also similar.

A shorter post crack development time will preserve the fresh sweetness.  In our experience, these types of alternative processed coffees can have a very quiet first crack.

name: Ecuador Loja El Dorado Green Gesha Lot 1 Anaerobic Washed Double Fermented 3x3
tags: anaerobic, ecuador, Ephemeral, gesha, Green Coffee, Rare, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Defined fragrance and aromas of jasmine, yuzu and mixed citrus. Up front notes of jasmine and peach with a lingering aftertaste of stone fruits, tannins and complimentary sugary sweetness. The acidity is well balanced and subtle with malic, lactic and citric acid noted. The cup is rounded out by a medium body with a creamy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: When roasting a Gesha coffee, we recommend a light roast that preserves the delicate floral notes.  This coffee is also incredibly dense, which will lend itself to a roast with intense heat application through early Maillard.

name: Guatemala Santa Rosa Finca Santa Ana Tafari Lavado
tags: Green Coffee, Guatemala, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of dark chocolate, florals and hazelnut. Notes of chamomile and milk chocolate with an aftertaste of citrus fruits and hazelnut. Marshmallow-like sweetness, medium-bright citric and lactic acidity with a medium body and creamy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: To best pull out the delicate floral notes in the fragrance and finish, we recommend a light roast.  High heat application and a higher charge temperature will bring out the complex citrus character in the coffee.

name: Ethiopia Guji Hambela Grade 1 Natural
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Natural Process, New Arrival
tasting_notes: Fragrance of strawberry and aroma of cooked fruit and dried dates. Notes of raspberry, strawberry and orange with an aftertaste of cocoa nibs. Cooked fruit-like sweetness, bright citric acidity and a medium-heavy body with syrupy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: This natural process Ethiopian coffee has loads of sweetness that can be developed by extending the caramelization phase of the roast.  A softer charge temperature and a bit of extending the drying time to allow for thorough heat penetration.  At a light temperature, the sweet berry jam flavors of this coffee will be most prominent.  As the coffee is developed more during the roasting process, the chocolatey cocoa nib character will come forward creating flavors of chocolate covered berries while the bright orange acidity will become more muted.

name: Rwanda Nyamasheke Muhororo Washed
tags: Green Coffee, Rwanda, Washed Process
farmer_grower: Celestin and Marie Rumenerangabo and 236 other households
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of brown sugar, dark chocolate, fresh cedar. Notes of cabernet sauvignon and dark chocolate with an aftertaste of grapefruit, florals and tannins. Medium malic, citric and lactic acidity. Medium body with creamy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: This coffee has a lot of delicate notes that will shine best in the range of light roasts (about 90 to 110 Agtron). Medium roasts will lose much of the floral notes and present a clean and sweet cup. You can read our Roast Approach blog on how to roast the 2025 Rwanda Nyamasheke Muhororo Washed coffee here.

name: El Salvador Ahuachapán Apaneca Finca La Fany Pacamara Washed
tags: El Salvador, Green Coffee, pacamara, washed, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of cocoa and lime blossom. Notes of white chocolate and florals with an aftertaste of lime and sugarcane sweetness. Bright citric acidity with a creamy mouthfeel and medium body.
roasting_notes: Pacamara coffees can be tricky to roast.  Going slower through the phases of Maillard and caramelization will help to improve body and reduce vegetal qualities that can be common in pacamaras.  Large beans, such as pacamaras, can be prone to roast defects such as scorching, tipping and facing.  Using a lower charge temperature and a longer time in drying can help to avoid roasting defects.  Going slower through the phases of Maillard and caramelization will help to improve body, reduce vegetal qualities that can be common in pacamaras, and develop sugars which will bring balance to the bright citric acidity.

name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Halo Beriti Grade 1 Washed
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, New Arrival, Washed Process
tasting_notes: Fragrance of florals and yuzu with an aroma of fresh pear.  Cup has clear notes of fresh peach, white tea, and chamomile.  The coffee has a medium, tea-like body and a bright complex acidity.  The citric, lactic, and malic acidity of the coffee is balanced with a white sugar sweetness.  The coffee finishes with notes of florals and oolong tea.
roasting_notes: For this dense Ethiopian coffee, we recommend that you start with a moderate charge temperature and an extended drying time.  This will provide you with more even heat penetration.  Use a high heat application through Maillard and into caramelization to develop the complex acidity and retain as much of the volatile florals as possible.

name: Ecuador Loja La Noria Green Gesha Lot 3 Washed
tags: anaerobic, ecuador, Ephemeral, gesha, Green Coffee, Rare, Washed Process
tasting_notes: This coffee leads with jasmine and grape aromatics, with cocoa, jasmine, and stone fruit flavor notes and a medium-intensity citric and malic acidity. The body is creamy and medium-heavy, with brown sugar sweetness and an aftertaste of citrus fruit and milk chocolate.
roasting_notes: When roasting a Gesha coffee, we recommend a light roast that preserves the delicate floral notes.  This coffee is also incredibly dense, which will lend itself to a roast with intense heat application through early Maillard.

name: Ethiopia Sidama Arbegona Duwancho Premium Washed
tags: Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Rare, Washed Process

roasting_notes: Coming soon!

name: Guatemala Huehuetenango HER Coffee
tags: Essentials, Green Coffee, Grounds for Health, Guatemala, HER, Perennial, Washed Process, women produced
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of dark chocolate and orange with up front flavors of chocolate, brown sugar sweetness, and nougat. Aftertaste of praline and orange blossom. Medium citric acidity with a creamy mouthfeel and medium body.
roasting_notes: Hacea’s expert roasting guidance for washed Huehuetenango coffees recommends maintaining a steady, moderate level of heat throughout the roast.  Few adjustments need to be made to the coffee, as it will roast steadily with consistent gas application. This method takes advantage of the bean’s natural density and consistent rate of rise, avoids stalling in post-crack development, and helps craft a smooth, chocolate-accented cup with balanced acidity and sweetness—the ideal expression for this Guatemalan coffee.

name: El Salvador Finca Colomba Oro Tinto Robusta Especial Honey
region: Los Naranjos, Ilamatepec, Santa Ana Department
tags: El Salvador, Essentials, Green Coffee, Honey Process, Robusta
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of cooked raspberry and cherry cordial.  Cup is full of dried fruit sweetness and a boozy cherry cordial flavor.  Sweet malty flavors and dark chocolate accent the mild orange citrus acidity.  Body is heavy with a creamy mouthfeel.
roasting_notes: Robustas are inherently more bitter and have an acidity that can be a bit harsh.  At a lighter roast, Robusta will taste more like a dark roast due to the fact that the coffee starts with more chlorogynic acid than Arabica.  Robustas work great in dark roasts, but may be best suited to using a post roast blend.  In a post roast blend, you can roast the Robusta to a light-medium roast level and have the flavors match your darker roasted Arabica.  You can read more about roasting this coffee in our full Roast Approach: Robusta here .

name: El Salvador Finca El Angel Pacamara Natural
tags: El Salvador, Ephemeral, Green Coffee, Natural, New Arrival
tasting_notes: Fragrance of cherry and pomegranate, aroma of blackberry, and strawberry jam. Notes of cocoa, red fruits and tropical fruits with an aftertaste of banana and dark chocolate and a milk chocolate sweetness. Mild malic acidity with a soft, creamy mouthfeel and medium body.
roasting_notes:
The large size of the Pacamara varietal can present some challenges with roasting, especially in developing sweetness.  It is important to approach this coffee with a gentle start that can allow heat to evenly penetrate the large seed.  This will also help to avoid the risk of scorching, which the large seed is prone to.  Pacamara coffees often have a bright acidity.  Extending the amount of time the coffee spends in the caramelization phase of the roast will help to develop sweetness and balance out the sharp acidity.  
We recommend roasting this coffee to a lighter roast level, with an approximate Agtron color reading of 90-85 in order to bring out the complex acidity and develop the sweetness.  This roast level corresponds to a post crack development time of between 1:20-1:35 and an end temperature of approximately 20-25 degrees Fahrenheit past first crack.

name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Aricha Adorsi Washed
region: Aricha Woreda, Yirgacheffe, Gedeo Zone, SNNPR
tags: Essentials, Ethiopia, Green Coffee, Perennial
tasting_notes: Fragrance and aroma of lemon blossom, lavender and panela. Notes of black tea and lemon with a floral and candied-lemon aftertaste and brown sugar sweetness. Bright citric acidity with a medium body and tea-like mouthfeel.
roasting_notes:
Dense coffees can handle a lot of heat application, and that heat helps build the momentum needed to push through the endothermic reactions of the Maillard and caramelization phases. With so much energy required later in the roast, it can be tempting to hit a dense coffee hard from the very start. However, it is also important that there is enough heat penetration through the coffee seed during drying. If heat doesn’t reach the center of the seed, the interior will be underdeveloped, leaving a cup with astringency and a lack of sweetness, even when the roast data looks right. Starting the roast with a minimal heat application allows heat to move evenly through the seed, while quickly increasing heat application after turnaround builds the energy needed heading into Maillard. This approach provides both adequate heat penetration and enough momentum to develop complex volatiles during Maillard, then carry that energy through caramelization for sweetness and body. The key with dense coffees is to think of the beginning of the roast as preparing the seed and the middle of the roast as driving it forward.  Strong heat application heading into Maillard can bring out bright, complex acidity and a clear expression of fruit. 

The challenge with washed coffees is balancing that acidity with enough sugar development. Extending time spent in caramelization builds sweetness and body, softening sharp acids into rounder fruit notes, while too much time there can mute the acidity that makes washed coffees shine.  How you approach caramelization will have a significant impact on your final cup.  A short time spent in caramelization will preserve complex acidity and florals, while leading to a thinner, more tea-like body.  Stretching out time spent in caramelization will reduce acids, but allow for more sugar and melanoidin (contributes to body) development.  Washed coffees also tend to have a more predictable and audible first crack than naturals or alternatively processed coffees, but it’s worth paying attention to how the coffee behaves after it. Some washed coffees will gently reduce their rate of rise on their own and do best with steady, consistent heat, while others will stall out if heat is pulled back too much and need some continued push to make it through development. 

In post crack development, a short time (85-100 seconds) will lead to a bright coffee with fresh fruit character and floral notes, with an Agtron color reading of between 90-85. This would commonly be considered a "light roast."  Extending the post crack development (100-150 seconds +) will bring out more notes of chocolate, cooked fruits, nuts, and spice, with an Agtron near the 80-70 mark.  This would lead to a roast that is commonly considered a "medium roast".
